tasks.short: Document progress against established speech-language objectives

steps.what: Review observed performance against the pathologist's established treatment objectives
Document descriptive progress against the specified objectives

loop.purpose: Draft a descriptive progress note without changing treatment objectives
loop.input: Assistant-checked observations tied to objective IDs and source sessions
loop.output: Draft retaining observed performance, assistance level and uncertainty
loop.check: Assistant checks every claim against session data, prompt level and objective wording; no inferred diagnosis or achieved-goal claim
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported progress claims or unclear objectives return to manual documentation and pathologist clarification
loop.why_not_simpler: Test fixed note templates first; varied session observations may need bounded narrative drafting

steps.what: Check and file the descriptive progress note within the delegated scope

tasks.design: Draft a descriptive note in the clinical record system {OTHER} from checked observations and established objective wording. The assistant verifies it within delegated scope; clinical interpretation, goal changes and any required pathologist sign-off remain with the pathologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Descriptive notes require repeated wording around measured performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded note drafting can assist composition without changing clinical responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: Prompting level and context can make a raw score misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant knows what actually happened in the session and recognises questions for the pathologist.
tasks.altitude: Less descriptive typing, with delegated scope unchanged.

reach.task: Flag a mismatch between recorded performance and objective wording
reach.learn: Objective definitions and clinical escalation boundaries

evidence.claim: Juvoly drafts consultation notes for clinician approval; this supports note-drafting capability, not validation for speech-language assistant progress documentation.
The assistant-note adaptation and time scenario are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is descriptive progress documentation, excluding raw performance-data collection in the separate data task and pathologist diagnosis or treatment decisions.

In s1 the assistant produces client/session ID, objective ID/version, observed performance, prompt or assistance level, source reference and uncertainty, retaining all 50 hours for review and capture. Missing objectives or unclear data require manual clarification, not inferred progress.

The pathologist produces established objectives through existing treatment planning. Any existing clinical review remains unchanged outside this assistant baseline. Test native note templates or dictation before a loop.
Allow four focal hours for template/failure upkeep and two other-role hours for pathologist review of the changed template; neither is free transferred work.
unknowns: Delegated documentation scope and required sign-off
research_questions: Does drafting preserve prompting level and objective wording without implying unobserved improvement?

already_counted.description: Observation review and final descriptive note check

incremental.description: Clinical review of changed note template

approvals.approved_version: Exact assistant note, client/session identity, objective version and source-data snapshot; changes require another assistant check and existing clinical review where required

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R88 gross12 minus4 focal upkeep =8 net; two other-role upkeep hours are separately declared. High assumes repetitive descriptive wording; low covers substantial correction. Clinical review and source capture remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and compile client performance data

steps.what: Collect clients' performance data using the pathologist's defined observation method
Compile observations into totals and specified performance summaries
Check compiled data against observations and flag quality concerns

tasks.design: Use a native session-data form and fixed summaries in the clinical record system {OTHER}, or checked formulas in {SPREADSHEET}. The assistant still observes and records responses and checks the compiled result; interpretation of treatment effectiveness remains with the pathologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collected response data can be counted and entered again in a summary table.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed formulas can compile explicitly defined response fields.
tasks.still_hard: Prompted responses, missing trials and changed measurement methods can invalidate comparison.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognises when an observation cannot be scored reliably.
tasks.altitude: Less manual compilation, with observation and checking intact.

reach.task: Explain data limitations before clinical interpretation

evidence.claim: Fixed compilation of assistant-captured speech-language data is an E1 model-knowledge design, not a measured capability case in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is data collection, compilation and data checking, excluding descriptive progress-note composition and clinical programme evaluation.

The assistant produces client/session ID, objective version, trial ID, response code, prompt level and missing-trial reason in s1, retaining all 60 hours for observation and capture. The existing pathologist supplies response definitions; absent or changed definitions trigger manual compilation and clarification.
Test native forms and formulas before code. No free structured response code is assumed and no model infers scores from audio.
Allow four focal hours for formula and data exception upkeep plus two other-role hours for review of changed measurement mappings.
unknowns: Observation definitions and current compilation method
research_questions: Do fixed summaries reproduce checked trial counts without treating missing or prompted responses as independent successes?

incremental.description: Clinical review of changed measurement mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gross25 minus4 focal upkeep =21 net, with two other-role hours separately counted. High assumes repeated manual compilation; low covers native existing summaries or inconsistent observations. Collection remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform session logistics and administrative support

steps.what: Prepare session equipment and maintain available supplies
Keep support records and coordinate activity scheduling within existing constraints

tasks.design: Retain physical resource preparation and the assistant's existing record and scheduling work in {DOCS} and {CALENDAR}. This broad support task does not establish duplicate entries or standard appointment rules that justify an automatic flow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support duties combine physical preparation and changing participant constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling tools support coordination without demonstrating a removable step.
tasks.still_hard: Availability, equipment and session needs can conflict.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices missing resources and resolves practical scheduling constraints.
tasks.altitude: Support responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Keeping unmeasured mixed support work unchanged is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is general session logistics, supplies and support records. Specific instructional-material preparation, clinical progress notes and performance-data compilation are assigned only to their separate tasks.
No free structured availability, par level or completed-session flag is assumed.
Existing native tools remain; no custom scheduler is proposed without a concrete booking baseline.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes.
unknowns: Actual support-duty mix and booking constraints
research_questions: Is there a specific repeated clerical transfer beyond the separately described note and data tasks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Physical preparation and current support administration retain time; no duplicate-entry baseline is inferred.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and prepare speech-language instructional materials

steps.what: Select instructional content and specify materials under the pathologist's plan
Prepare printable cards or worksheets from selected words, pictures and instructions
Check material fidelity and prepare the final physical session materials

tasks.design: Configure a fixed card or worksheet template in {DOCS} using exact selected content from approved sources. Keep content suitability, final checks and physical preparation with the assistant under the pathologist's existing direction; the generator does not choose treatment stimuli.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected material can require repeated page layout before use.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can place exact words and pictures without generating clinical content.
tasks.still_hard: Small changes to a word, picture or prompt can alter the intended activity.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognises whether the result matches the planned objective and client access needs.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive layout, with clinical direction and material suitability unchanged.

reach.task: Flag a mismatch between prepared stimuli and the planned activity
reach.learn: Stimulus selection boundaries and accessible formats

evidence.claim: Exact-content worksheet and card layout is an E1 design from model knowledge; no digest source validates automatic speech-therapy material selection.

assumptions: Boundary is selecting and preparing specific instructional material, excluding general room preparation and supplies in the support task.

The pathologist produces the activity plan through existing clinical work. In s1 the assistant selects and captures objective version, exact words, image files, instructions, order, text size and page format; all 60 hours remain. Missing approved content returns to manual preparation and clinical clarification.
Test native templates before custom code. No free structured therapeutic-suitability flag or model-generated stimuli are assumed.
Allow four focal hours for template and formatting exceptions and two other-role hours for pathologist review of changed template conventions beyond existing routine direction.
unknowns: Current layout burden and approved content sources
research_questions: Does the template preserve exact stimuli and accessibility requirements in the printed material?

already_counted.description: Content selection, capture, fidelity check and physical preparation

incremental.description: Clinical review of changed material conventions

approvals.approved_version: Exact material proof, selected stimuli, activity-plan version and client access format; changes require another assistant check and clinical clarification if needed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gross25 minus4 focal upkeep =21 net; two other-role upkeep hours separately declared. High assumes repetitive layout; low covers existing templates or complex physical materials. Clinical selection and physical work retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce descriptive note wording, repeated data compilation and material layout while preserving observation, delegated scope and pathologist direction.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who supplies reliable observations and faithful materials while keeping clinical decisions with the speech-language pathologist.
